page.title: Best Z-Wave Outdoor Plug (2026): Minoston MP22Z vs Zooz ZEN05 800LR
page.desc: The best Z-Wave outdoor plug for most homes is the Minoston MP22Z: 800-series, IP65, 15 A and rated to -4°F. When Zooz's ZEN05 800LR, the MP22ZD dimmer or a dual plug fits better.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best z-wave outdoor plug is the Minoston MP22Z ({buy:minoston-mp22z-z-wave-800-outdoor-plug}): Z-Wave 800 series with Long Range, IP65, 15 A / 1,875 W, and Minoston rates it for -4°F to 122°F, so holiday lights keep answering the hub through a northern December. The closest rival, the Zooz ZEN05 800LR (about a dollar more at The Smartest House on 2026-11-06), adds live power reporting and a 5-year registered warranty, but Zooz rates it for only 32°F to 104°F and says you will likely lose Z-Wave control in hard cold.

Both plugs need a Z-Wave hub (SmartThings, Hubitat, Home Assistant, HomeSeer, Ring Alarm). Neither pairs directly with an Echo. Both use the 800-series chip with S2 security and SmartStart, and both reach up to 1,300 ft in the open if your hub supports Z-Wave Long Range. In Long Range mode a plug does not repeat for other devices, so it will not strengthen the rest of your mesh.

Pick the Zooz ZEN05 800LR if you live where winters stay above freezing and you want the hub to confirm the lights actually drew power. Pick the Minoston MP22ZD ({buy:minoston-mp22zd-z-wave-800-outdoor-dimmer-plug}) if you want to dim patio string lights: it is the only outdoor-rated Z-Wave dimmer plug on the 800 series, with 400 W incandescent or 150 W dimmable LED. For two loads from one receptacle, the Minoston MP24Z ({buy:minoston-mp24z-z-wave-800-outdoor-dual-plug}) and the Zooz ZEN14 800LR cost about the same; the Minoston carries the -4°F rating, the Zooz the longer warranty.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Dropped or ignored commands is the most common complaint across Zooz's support articles and the SmartThings, Homey and openHAB forums. Outdoor plugs sit at the edge of the mesh, often behind brick, stucco or foil-backed insulation. Pair the plug indoors near the hub first, then move it outside, and add a mains-powered Z-Wave device near the wall it hangs on if it still misses commands. Cold is the second theme: Zooz's own FAQ says the ZEN05 is not rated below 32°F, and forum users in the Northeast ask for a cold-rated plug every holiday season. Water and insects come third: three Minoston owners on Amazon note there is no gasket at the cord entry, and one dimmer died after a year when bugs got inside. Hang any of these plugs vertically, under an eave or a bubble cover, at least a foot off the ground. Last, hub support: the dual-outlet Minoston models show as a single switch on Homey and need Minoston's driver on Hubitat.

Which one by need

  • Holiday and landscape lights where it freezes: Minoston MP22Z. Same chip and IP65 rating as the Zooz, a lower price, and the -4°F rating.
  • Power reporting or a long warranty, mild climate: Zooz ZEN05 800LR. Live wattage lets an automation confirm the lights came on, and registration brings a 5-year warranty.
  • Dimming string lights: Minoston MP22ZD. No other outdoor Z-Wave dimmer plug ships on the 800 series. Keep LED strings under 150 W.
  • Two loads from one outlet: Minoston MP24Z if it freezes, Zooz ZEN14 800LR if you want the Zooz warranty. Both share one 15 A limit.

Not recommended

Used or old-stock Minoston MP22Z units on the 500-series chip: they were rated only 32°F to 104°F and lack Long Range, and some early threads describe flaky behavior. The Enbrighten Z-Wave Long Range outdoor plug costs more, publishes no temperature rating and was sold out at Jasco on 2026-11-06. The Eva Logik ZW97 dual plug has owners on two hubs reporting that only one outlet registers. Avoid any plug-in dimmer for pumps, motors or heaters, and keep heaters off every outdoor smart plug.
